title: SQS & SNS: Queues, Fan-out and Decoupling
summary: Buffer work with SQS, broadcast with SNS, and combine them for fan-out.
tldr: **SQS** is a pull-based buffer: producers keep working when consumers are slow or down, and workers scale on queue depth. One message goes to **one** consumer.

**SNS** pushes each message to **every** subscriber. **SNS → one SQS queue per consumer** is the classic fan-out: each service gets a copy, works at its own pace and can go offline without losing events.
Migrating an app that speaks **JMS, AMQP, MQTT or OpenWire** without code changes? Use **Amazon MQ** (ActiveMQ or RabbitMQ), not SQS.

keyFacts.text: Hides a received message from other consumers while it is processed (default 30 s, max 12 h). For Lambda, set it to at least **6×** the function timeout.
Maximum **long polling** wait (`ReceiveMessageWaitTimeSeconds`). It cuts empty responses and cost compared with short polling.
Maximum message retention (default 4 days). A **dead-letter queue** catches messages after `maxReceiveCount` failures; **DLQ redrive** sends them back after a fix.
Maximum delivery delay, set per queue (**delay queue**) or per message (**message timer**) on standard queues.
Maximum SQS message size. Larger payloads (up to 2 GB) go through the **SQS Extended Client Library**, which stores the body in S3.

traps: Several consumers polling **one** SQS queue split the messages between them; none gets every message.
Standard SQS queues have no message priority. Use separate queues for priority tiers.
Raising the visibility timeout to the longest possible job delays retries when a worker crashes.
A delay of hours or days can't be done with SQS delays (15 min max); use EventBridge Scheduler.
SNS alone doesn't buffer for an offline consumer. Put an SQS queue behind each subscription.
Amazon SQS doesn't speak JMS/OpenWire or AMQP natively, so it means application code changes.
